entries.title: Create a new customer
entries.answer: New customer creates the restaurant in Booqy: it invites the owner, opens their Stripe account and sets up their website, with no deploy needed.
steps: Open New customer in the menu (or press + New customer on Customers).
Fill in 1 Restaurant company: name, slug, legal name, org. number and address.
Fill in 2 Owner login: the owner gets an email with a temporary password for the restaurant admin app.
Fill in 3 Contact & communication, then pick the plan under 4 Plan and the terms under 4b Invoicing.
Add the locations, then press Create customer. The page follows the setup until it is done.
entries.suggestion: How do I add a new customer?

entries.title: Find a customer
entries.answer: Customers lists every restaurant on the platform. Search by name, slug, owner email or domain, and use the status chips (Active is chosen first) to see offboarded or suspended customers.
steps: Open Customers in the menu.
Type in the search field, or press a status chip such as All, Suspended or Offboarded.
Click a row to open the customer's page.

entries.title: Change a customer's plan, price or features
entries.answer: A customer's plan, monthly price, limits and features are on the Plan tab of their page. Limits take effect at once; a changed plan or price is invoiced from the next month.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Plan tab.
Pick the plan, and change Locations allowed, Monthly price, SEK ex VAT, the limits or the Features checkboxes if needed.
Press Save plan.

entries.title: Give a customer the Free plan
entries.answer: Free has no monthly charge and Growth's features. Pick Free on the Plan tab (or in step 4 of New customer): it lasts three months by default (a new end date is at least 14 days ahead), or tick No end date. The owner gets an email 14 days before it ends, and the day after it the customer moves to the plan in Then switch to, at Price after Free (an own price stays). If the email could not go out in time, the free period runs until 14 days after it does. Change the date, the plan or the price any time.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Plan tab and pick Free.
Set Free until (or tick No end date) and Then switch to.
Press Save plan.

entries.title: Add a location
entries.answer: Locations are on the Locations tab of the customer's page. When the plan's limit is reached, adding one offers to raise the limit by one, or you change the plan on the Plan tab.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Locations tab, then + Add location.
Fill in Name, Address, Phone and Email and save.
At the limit: press Raise limit and add, or raise Locations allowed on the Plan tab.

entries.title: Invite another owner
entries.answer: Owners are invited on the Users tab of the customer's page. The new owner gets a temporary password by email. Owners invite their own staff from the restaurant admin app.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Users tab.
Under Invite another owner, fill in Name and Business email.
Press Send invite.

entries.title: Stripe onboarding link for a restaurant
entries.answer: Each restaurant has its own Stripe account connected to the platform. On the Payments tab you see whether it can take payments, create an onboarding link for the owner and check the status with Stripe. No keys are exchanged.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Payments tab.
Press Create onboarding link, then Copy or Open it (it expires within minutes).
When the owner is done, press Check status with Stripe: Can take payments turns to Yes.

entries.title: Customers waiting for Stripe
entries.answer: The Payments column on Customers shows Ready or Not ready for each customer.

live.text: {value} active customers can't take card payments yet: their Stripe setup isn't finished. The Payments column on Customers shows which.
live.countText: {value} active {customer can't|customers can't} take card payments yet: their Stripe setup isn't finished. The Payments column on Customers shows which.

entries.title: Number of customers
entries.answer: The number of customers stands under the heading on Customers.

live.text: There are {value} customers on the platform, counting every status.
live.countText: There {is|are} {value} {customer|customers} on the platform, counting every status.

entries.title: Active customers
entries.answer: The Active chip on Customers counts the active customers.

entries.title: Customers whose setup failed
entries.answer: The Setup failed chip on Customers lists them. On the customer's page, Retry setup (or Fix) runs it again.
steps: Open Customers and press the Setup failed chip.
Click the customer and press Retry setup, or Fix to correct the field that stopped it.

entries.title: Add a domain for a restaurant
entries.answer: Domains are added on the Domains tab of the customer's page: buy a new domain in the restaurant's name, connect one they already have (they switch the name servers) or add just a CNAME for www. Until then the site answers on its booqy.se address.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Domains tab, then Add domain.
Choose Buy a new domain, Connect a domain they already have or Just a CNAME, and follow the steps.

entries.title: A restaurant's website
entries.answer: Each restaurant's website has its own repo. The Website tab of the customer's page shows the repo and deploys, where the site answers, how to run it locally, gives a GitHub user access and archives the repo.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Website tab.
Under Give access, type the GitHub username and press Invite.

entries.title: Website visitors (booqy.se)
entries.answer: Website under Numbers shows the visitors to booqy.se, counted without cookies: countries, devices, sources and more for the period you pick.
steps: Open Website in the menu.
Pick a period, or set your own dates.

entries.title: Add an operator
entries.answer: Operators are the people who can sign in to Booqy Console; everyone has the same rights. A new operator gets an email with a temporary password (valid for 3 days), chooses their own password on first sign-in and sets up an authenticator app.
steps: Open Operators in the menu.
Press + Add operator.
Fill in Name and Email and press Send invite.
entries.suggestion: How do I add another operator?

entries.title: Two-step sign-in with an authenticator app
entries.answer: Every operator signs in with an email, a password and a 6-digit code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Microsoft Authenticator). The app is set up on the first sign-in by scanning a QR code.
steps: Sign in with your email and password.
The first time: choose your password, scan the QR code with the authenticator app and enter the 6-digit code it shows.
After that: enter the 6-digit code for Booqy Console at each sign-in.

entries.title: Disable, delete or re-invite an operator
entries.answer: Each operator's row on Operators has Edit, Resend invite, Disable or Enable, and Delete. You can't disable or delete yourself or the last active operator.
steps: Open Operators in the menu.
Use the buttons on the operator's row.

entries.title: Send news to the restaurant owners
entries.answer: Mail sends news to every active customer's owner, from Booqy with replies to support. Send yourself a test first; a send can't be recalled.
steps: Open Mail in the menu (Compose is open).
Write the Subject and the Message.
Press Send me a test and check it.
Press Send to N owners and confirm.

entries.title: The mail brand template
entries.answer: The Brand template tab on Mail sets how the news looks: sender name, reply-to address, accent colour, logo, signature and footer line.
steps: Open Mail and press Brand template.
Change what you need and press Save template.

entries.title: Sent news
entries.answer: The Sent tab on Mail lists every send, who it went to and what happened.
steps: Open Mail and press Sent.
Click a send to see its recipients.

entries.title: The mail outbox (dev)
entries.answer: In dev the Outbox keeps what the platform would have emailed, plus a copy of every SMS, instead of sending it, for 30 days. Click a message to read it as HTML or text, with its links.
steps: Open Outbox from Cmd K, or Mail and then Outbox.
Click a message; Load older shows more.

entries.title: Emails in the outbox
entries.answer: The Outbox lists the messages of the last 30 days, newest first.

live.text: The outbox has {value} messages from the last 30 days.
live.countText: The outbox has {value} {message|messages} from the last 30 days.

entries.title: Finance overview
entries.answer: Finance shows MRR, paying customers, collected and outstanding money, gross margin, revenue, AWS cost and unit economics per billing period (25th to 24th), in SEK ex VAT. Pick a customer to see just them, and export the rows as CSV.
steps: Open Finance in the menu.
Pick the Billing period and how many periods.
Use Export customers (CSV) or Export daily (CSV) for the rows.

entries.title: MRR
entries.answer: MRR is the first figure on Finance.

live.text: MRR is {value} right now (SEK ex VAT, this billing period).

entries.title: Paying customers
entries.answer: Paying customers stands next to MRR on Finance.

live.text: {value} customers are paying this billing period.
live.countText: {value} {customer is|customers are} paying this billing period.

entries.title: Outstanding money
entries.answer: Outstanding is on Finance, next to Collected.

live.text: {value} is invoiced but not paid yet this billing period.

entries.title: Run invoicing
entries.answer: Invoices are created on the 25th for the period from the 25th to the 24th (the monthly price; SMS are included, Free has no charge). After a missed 25th you run it by hand on Finance, Payments, with a preview first.
steps: Open Finance and press Payments.
Press Run invoicing and check the preview.
Press Create these invoices.

entries.title: Overdue invoices and reminders
entries.answer: Finance, Payments shows who has paid for a month, with reminders and fees. Unpaid invoices get weekly reminders by themselves, the statutory late fee after the grace period and interest when paid; past due too long means suspension until paid. Send reminder sends one at once.
steps: Open Finance and press Payments.
Pick the month and press the Overdue chip.
Press Send reminder on the invoice's row.

entries.title: Start or end a customer's agreement
entries.answer: A customer's agreement and invoices are on the Billing tab of their page: start it, send a card link (Stripe Checkout, valid 24 hours), charge a saved card, convert a try-out to a subscription or cancel it.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Billing tab.
Press Start agreement and choose Try-out period or Subscription, or use Create card link, Charge the card or Cancel agreement.

entries.title: Suspend or resume a customer
entries.answer: Suspending signs out and blocks every user and shows the website as unavailable; nothing is deleted, and Resume undoes it at any time.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Suspend or offboard tab.
Write a Reason (kept in the activity log) and press Suspend customer. Resume customer brings them back.

entries.title: Offboard, restore or delete a customer
entries.answer: Offboarding signs out and blocks every user, takes the website and its domains offline, archives the website repo and ends the subscription. Restore brings everything back until the retention period is over (90 days in production); after that, or at once with Delete customer, the data and the website repo are deleted for good.
steps: Open Customers and click the customer.
Press the Suspend or offboard tab.
Type the customer's slug to confirm and press Offboard customer.
To undo: Restore customer on the same tab, while it is still restorable.

entries.title: A customer's activity log
entries.answer: The Activity tab on the customer's page lists the latest 25 events.
steps: Open Customers, click the customer and press Activity.

entries.title: Light or dark mode
entries.answer: Light or dark is under Settings, Appearance and sound. Press to switch; light is the default. It is kept in this browser.
steps: Open Settings.
Under Appearance and sound, press Light or dark.

entries.title: Background behind the glass
entries.answer: Background under Settings sets what sits behind the glass: Colour (the Booqy backdrop, the swatches Wine, Walnut, Sand, Sage, Slate and Plum, or your own colour with +) or Your image, a picture you upload. In the desktop app there is also See-through, the default, with your desktop showing through.
steps: Open Settings.
Under Background, press Colour, Your image (or See-through in the desktop app).
Pick a swatch or + for your own colour, or press Choose picture and pick a JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC image.
entries.suggestion: How do I change the background?

entries.title: Click sound and volume
entries.answer: Click sound and Volume are under Settings, Appearance and sound. The click is on by default; 40 % is the standard volume and 0 % is silent.
steps: Open Settings.
Press Click sound to turn it off or on, or move Volume.

entries.title: Download the desktop app
entries.answer: Booqy Console is also an app in its own window, with the same sign-in and features. Settings, Desktop app (Download app in the menu) suggests the file for your computer and lists the rest for Mac, Windows and Linux. It isn't signed yet, so the computer warns once: Opening it the first time explains what to press.
steps: Press Download app in the menu, or open Settings and go to Desktop app.
Press the recommended download, or pick the file for your computer from the list.
Open it; on a Mac, use Open Anyway in System Settings, Privacy & Security the first time.

entries.title: Search and commands
entries.answer: Cmd K (Ctrl K on Windows and Linux) or the Search field opens the command palette: actions, every page and your recent pages. Arrows choose, Enter opens, Esc closes.
